status: mechanism_only - use_output_fusion=False in every arm, so the LLM reaches the GNN ONLY through the consultative feedback path. NOT comparable to results/unsw_nb15_current.json (fusion on).
question: Does edge injection (--injection-mode edge, the canonical default) still causally use the LLM's advice under v2 encoding and the canonical top_k/scale (31.0/2.0), now that the loop-fusion fairness fix has landed? Supersedes results/unsw_nb15_edge_injection.json, which was measured pre-v2 under a different mechanism-only variant.
verdict: PARTLY RETRACTED 2026-08-30 -- see `retraction` below. The original verdict read: 'YES. real > control_head_only > control_shuffled > control_random, on both UNSW and ToN-IoT.' The real-vs-control leg does NOT replicate under a thread-pinned re-run and must not be cited. What still holds: the mechanism is sensitive to advice CONTENT (shuffled and random both degrade beyond drift, except UNSW shuffled which is unresolved). What does NOT hold: that real advice measurably beats no advice.

retraction.cause: This run was NOT thread-pinned. OMP_NUM_THREADS/MKL_NUM_THREADS were unset and torch.set_num_threads(1) was not called; the runner only began pinning them on 2026-08-30. Documented drift at fixed seed without pinning is ~0.012 macro-F1, which exceeds the real-vs-control effect this experiment reports.

replication.source: results/{unsw_nb15,ton_iot}_oracle_ceiling_v2.json (Gate 0, thread-pinned, same 3 seeds, same top_k/scale, same pooled_5_fold_oof_macro_f1 metric)
replication.reading: Absolute levels moved 0.012-0.016 between runs and real_minus_control flipped sign on UNSW (+0.0064 -> -0.0016) while growing on ToN (+0.0026 -> +0.0130). Not a systematic bias in either direction -- the effect is not resolvable at this sample size.

retraction.still_supported: The mechanism reads advice CONTENT. control_random degrades beyond drift on both datasets (-0.0518 UNSW, -0.0593 ToN) and control_shuffled does on ToN (-0.0228). UNSW's control_shuffled (-0.0098) is inside the drift band and is unresolved.
retraction.no_longer_supported: 'real > control_head_only', and therefore the full 4-arm ordering. Do not cite this file as proof that the LLM is a working consultant. Gate 0 independently finds the canonical prototype consultant captures approximately 0% of available mechanism headroom (UNSW -4.5%, ToN 11.9%, neither separated from zero).
retraction.if_rerunning: Export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. src/pipeline/step4/mechanism_only_edge_injection.py now pins this itself, but that pin postdates this run. A thread-pinned 4-arm re-run (adding shuffled/random, which Gate 0 did not measure) is the experiment that would settle the shuffled leg on UNSW.

arms.control_head_only: feedback structurally absent (bias term not added); the correct no-mechanism baseline, never the bare GNN rung
arms.real: true whitened-prototype advice delivered to the consulted edge
arms.control_shuffled: real advice delivered to the WRONG edge
arms.control_random: fixed uniform noise in place of advice

pass_criterion: real > control_head_only AND both advice controls <= control_head_only. Reported as met on both datasets at the time; the 'real > control_head_only' half is RETRACTED (see `retraction`) -- it does not replicate under thread pinning. The 'advice controls <= control_head_only' half still holds.
reproduce: python -m src.pipeline.step4.mechanism_only_edge_injection (requires prototypes.pt and folds.pt already built for both datasets). Writes results/raw/mechanism_only_v2.json; raw per-arm output and console log are committed at results/raw/mechanism_only_v2.{json,log}.

supersedes.reason: That file measured a different mechanism-only variant (edge_prototype/edge_trained_head/attention arms, pre-v2 encoding, injection_scale swept 10-100) and is not re-verified on v2. This file is the v2, canonical-top_k/scale, 4-control-arm re-run, on both datasets.

caveats: 3-seed means; std 0.01-0.03 on both datasets, so the real-vs-control point gain (+0.006 UNSW, +0.003 ToN) is smaller than one seed's noise band. The ordering across all 4 arms, not the magnitude of the top gap, is the load-bearing evidence here.

control_random has by far the highest churn (0.042 UNSW, 0.109 ToN) yet the lowest score -- noise perturbs predictions the most while making them worse, which is itself evidence the mechanism is not simply capacity-limited.
Not comparable to results/unsw_nb15_current.json or results/ton_iot_current.json: those runs have output fusion ON, this experiment has it OFF in every arm by design.
